bull_bear.body:
- India's and Asia's largest dialysis chain; over 50% share of India's organized dialysis market (treatments), ~4.4x next largest provider (FY24 revenue)
- Only Indian dialysis provider scaled internationally; 519 clinics across 4 countries
- Scalable, asset-light, capital-efficient model (52.41% clinics on revenue-sharing)
- Protocol-led clinical excellence (RenAssure), proprietary tech (Renova, patient apps), Enpidia training academy
- Proven acquisition and integration track record (18 companies acquired)
- Patient-centric leadership backed by marquee PE/VC investors
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Captive clinic contract dependence — Captive clinics were 43.30% of revenue FY25 (62.23% FY23); cancellation/non-renewal of hospital arrangements could materially hurt revenue
- Reimbursement / regulated pricing — Prices depend on recommended/mandatory fees; Philippine and Uzbekistan reimbursement frameworks subject to periodic revision
- Acquisition and integration risk — Growth relies on acquisitions (18 done); integration failures could hurt returns; some subsidiaries loss-making
- Geographic concentration — Substantial revenue from southern India clinics; international ops carry FX and regulatory exposure
- Key personnel / promoter concentration — Dependence on founder Vikram Vuppala; corporate promoters lack line-of-business experience
- Accreditation dependence — Loss of NABH/JCI/PhilHealth accreditation could impact revenue
- Third-party payer / receivables risk — Financial difficulties of payers may cause payment delays or write-offs
- Regulatory / FEMA compliance — Past delays in RBI/FEMA filings; extensive licensing requirements
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: NephroPlus offers comprehensive dialysis care through a network of clinics spanning diagnosis, treatment and wellness programs, including haemodialysis, home and mobile dialysis, supported by pharmacy. It operates in-hospital captive clinics, standalone clinics and government PPP formats across India and internationally (Philippines, Uzbekistan, Nepal), serving patients with End Stage Renal Disorder.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Core dialysis:** Haemodialysis, Home haemodialysis, Hemodiafiltration, Continuous renal replacement therapy, Plasmapheresis
- **Off-clinic / accessibility:** Holiday dialysis, Dialysis on call, Dialysis on wheels
- **Ancillary:** Pharmacy / dialysis-related pharmacy products, Renova dialyzer reprocessing system, RenAssure protocols, Enpidia training academy

outlook.body:
- Continue to consolidate leadership position in India by opening new clinics (167 new clinics via IPO proceeds)
- Selectively pursue strategic acquisitions and investments in Philippines, Uzbekistan and other key markets
- Deepen patient reach and geographic footprint in India, Philippines, Nepal and Uzbekistan

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Company intends to open 167 new dialysis clinics in India (69 greenfield, 98 brownfield) across ~0.19 million sq ft, funded partly by IPO net proceeds (Rs 1,291.06 million), over Fiscals 2026-2028, targeting states including Rajasthan, UP, Delhi, Telangana, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and others. Internationally, it plans to continue inorganic expansion in the Philippines and Uzbekistan and grow via the KSA joint venture. It scaled from 1 clinic in 2010 to 519 clinics by Sep 30, 2025.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Expansion of clinic network and treatment volumes drives revenue
- Recurring revenue from chronic, life-sustaining nature of dialysis
- Consumables cost reduction (from 32.59% of revenue FY23 to 23.05% in H1FY26) improving margins
- Rising share of international revenue (11.70% FY23 to 31.79% FY25) at higher price points
- Operating leverage from scale in procurement and utilisation (utilisation rate 68.63% FY23 to 74.99% H1FY26)
- Faster breakeven for captive/brownfield (3-4 months) vs greenfield (12 months)

It reaches guests through in-hospital captive clinics, standalone clinics and government-backed public-private partnerships (PPP) across India, Nepal, the Philippines, Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabia (via a JV).

Acquired clinics typically reach operational breakeven in three to four months versus roughly twelve months for a greenfield clinic. risks.note: Per-session dialysis costs range from Rs 1,000-3,500, creating a financial burden for patients; lack of comprehensive insurance or low income limits access and increases mortality risk, impacting patient volumes.
risks.risk: High treatment costs and affordability constraints

risks.note: Approximately 90% of dialysis facilities are located in urban areas while rural and semi-urban populations remain underserved; over 60% of patients travel more than 50 km for hemodialysis.

India has approximately 2,600 nephrologists (1.90 per million population versus a global median of 9.95 per million), alongside a severe shortage of dialysis technicians and nurses and high attrition rates.

Only about 50% of Indian dialysis patients receive the WHO-recommended three treatments per week (47% receive two, the remainder one); poor adherence worsens outcomes and constrains revenue per patient.

Complexity in regulatory approvals, delayed empanelment under government health schemes, and potential changes to reimbursement rates (PM-JAY, PhilHealth, Uzbekistan government rates) may impact revenue predictability.
Operations across diverse regulatory, currency and cultural environments in the Philippines, Uzbekistan, KSA and Nepal expose the Company to execution, integration, currency and political risks.
Increasing digital integration of patient records, IoT-enabled machines and teleconsultation platforms heightens cyber risk and data-privacy obligations across multiple jurisdictions.
